newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by ongoing slaughter cutbacks and sluggish pork demand, livestock dealers said.
Several key pork packing companies reported slaughter cutbacks for the third consecutive week due to unprofitable operating margins, company and market sources said.

Margins have been pushed deep into the red by slow pork demand and high hog prices, they said. But cash hog prices have been underpinned somewhat by a seasonal reduction in supplies and by spring planting, some sources noted.
Pork cut-out prices on Friday were quoted down $0.79 to $0.82 per cwt, USDA statistics showed.

Central carlot pork prices at midday on Monday were quoted steady to $1.00 per cwt lower on hams and $3.00 to $5.00 lower on pork bellies. There were 30 loads of pork cuts reported sold and six loads of trimmed, processed pork, USDA said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants could range $56.00 to $56.50 and Illinois top hog prices could range $55.50 to $56.00, packer buyers and livestock dealers in those areas said. Indiana/Ohio top prices at plants could range $56.00 to $56.50, sources there said.
